question: Does recombination beat mutation when the gate is a Lean proof?
why_now: A verified answer needs a formal gate, and the gate used to cost one Lean invocation per candidate. It now costs one per BATCH, because a compile reports a per-declaration verdict even when it exits nonzero, which brings a paired experiment inside a few minutes.

architecture.fitness: exact rational agreement at sample points, in Python, zero Lean cost
architecture.why_separate: A wrong fitness misguides the search and wastes effort but can never cause a wrong acceptance, since nothing is accepted without a proof whose axioms line is free of sorryAx and of non-whitelisted axioms. Fitness guides, the kernel decides.

controls.pairing: identical seeds and identical initial populations in both arms

lean_gate.isolation_strategy: none needed: one invocation yields a per-candidate verdict, since a failed proof is admitted as sorryAx and reported by name

statistics.pre_registered_criterion: crossover's paired median ratio must be <= 0.90 to support recombination

conclusion.headline: Recombination does not help, and it significantly HURTS the probability of solving at all. Mutation-only solved 94/200 (47.0%) against crossover's 58/200 (29.0%), Fisher exact p = 2.98e-04.
conclusion.the_two_measures_disagree_and_that_is_th: Conditional on solving, crossover changes the evaluation count hardly at all (median ratio 0.959, cheaper on 18 of 35 pairs, sign test p = 1.000). So crossover does not make successful searches faster; it makes success less likely. That is the signature of a macromutation that destroys assembled structure rather than a recombination that transmits it, which is independently what hypothesis AR.H3-gp proposed on different evidence.
conclusion.why_this_closes_the_line: Papers F, G and H and hypothesis AR.H1-gp established that recombination is not DETECTABLE in evolved programs, because no heritable character carries it. This establishes the prior question from the other side: recombination does not HELP either. Both follow from one cause -- a program's contribution is not modular, so swapping subtrees is macromutation. Four independent refutations now agree.
conclusion.honest_note_against_an_earlier_number_of: At 48 seeds the paired median ratio was 1.500 on 10 pairs, which would have been reported as crossover being 50% more expensive. At 200 seeds and 35 pairs it is 0.959 and the sign test is p = 1.000. The small-n paired estimate did not replicate. The solve-rate difference, which was p = 0.147 at 48 seeds, is the measure that held up.

not_established: One grammar ({+,-,*} over h,w,q,p and three constants), one target rung (L3, size 9), one budget (4000 evaluations), one population scheme (steady-state, tournament of 3), one crossover rate (0.5). The result is about THIS search, not about recombination in general.

The arms' RNG streams diverge after the initial population, since the crossover arm consumes an extra draw for its crossover decision. Pairing is therefore on the initial population, not on the whole stream; 200 seeds is what carries the comparison rather than a matched trace.
The discriminating rung was chosen by a pooled-solve-rate band of [0.3, 0.7] fixed in advance. Only L3 fell in it, so there is no second rung to check the result against.
The full Verlet target (L6, size 17) was solved 0/16 by both arms at this budget, so nothing is established at the size the rung-2 gate actually cares about.
